Demo CTI report for deterministic offline extraction.

Example Group (G1001), also known as Example Alias and Cozy Bear, conducted a
phishing-focused operation against a fictional financial organisation. The
report records only explicit indicators and ATT&CK identifiers. It does not
make an attribution beyond the explicit group reference above. Analysts should
retain the source report and the local ATT&CK bundle used for validation.

Initial delivery used a message sent from alerts@example.org to an employee at
security@example.test. The message referenced https://portal.example.test/login
and https://updates.example.test/download. The same campaign later used the
defanged domain evil[.]example and the hostname cdn.example.test. DNS telemetry
also recorded 198.51.100.10, 198.51.100.11, 203.0.113.50, and the IPv6 address
2001:db8::10. The two public addresses were repeated in several endpoint and
proxy records. The observed user agent was not used as a detection conclusion.

The attachment was assessed through the explicit techniques T1566.001 and
T1059. The report also contains T1059.001, T1027, T1071.001, T1105, T1082,
T1003, T1047, and T1486. T1566.001 appeared twice in the source material and
T1059.001 appeared twice in the source material. These IDs must be validated
against the local Enterprise ATT&CK bundle before any enrichment is shown.
No technique is inferred from prose, process names, URLs, or addresses.

Endpoint analysis identified the sample SHA-256
0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef, SHA-1
0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567, and MD5
0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef. A later object had SHA-256
abcdefabcdefabcdefabcdefabcdefabcdefabcdefabcdefabcdefabcdefabcd. The same
first SHA-256 was copied into two analyst notes. The file names are preserved
only as local observations and are not used for semantic matching.

Network controls observed http://evil.example/path, https://evil.example/path,
http://198.51.100.10/a, and https://cdn.example.test/assets. A duplicate URL
https://updates.example.test/download was observed by a second sensor. The
report also lists the defanged address hxxps://evil[.]example/path as an
observed form. Normalisation may retain the raw and normalised representations
without changing the source evidence.

The operator used a scripting interpreter under T1059.001 and transferred a
payload under T1105. Discovery activity explicitly referenced T1082. Credential
access explicitly referenced T1003. Remote execution explicitly referenced
T1047. Obfuscated content explicitly referenced T1027. Application layer
communications explicitly referenced T1071.001. Data impact explicitly
referenced T1486. The parent identifier T1059 is also present as an explicit
identifier. These statements intentionally repeat IDs so that occurrence counts
can be tested without adding analytical inference.

The second section names Second Group (G1002) as a separate explicit mention.
It does not claim that Second Group performed the operation. The group name is
present to test exact-name and ATT&CK ID handling. Example Malware (S1001) is
also named as a local ATT&CK software record. Its mention is not a conclusion
about deployment in the target organisation.

The organisation reported CVE-2024-0001, CVE-2024-0002, and CVE-2023-9999 in
its ticketing system. These CVEs are extraction candidates, not exploit claims.
The email support@example.org and the domain reports.example.test appeared in
the same ticket. Another email, response@example.net, was included in an
analyst contact field. These data points must remain exact strings in Excel and
must never be interpreted as formulas.

For reproducibility, the report contains repeated indicators: evil[.]example,
198.51.100.10, T1566.001, T1059.001, and CVE-2024-0001. The output should show
unique values and occurrence counts. It should show text-based warnings when a
report has too few explicit TTPs, but this rich fixture deliberately contains
many explicit TTPs. The resulting dashboard should therefore show IOC types,
techniques, tactics, and non-attributive group overlap where local data exists.

All conclusions in this fixture are bounded by the local data model. No country,
sector, region, motivation, campaign, or confidence value is implied by the
descriptions. Sector and region outputs remain dependent on explicit YAML
mapping. Sigma coverage remains dependent only on exact ATT&CK tags. Multi-
report corroboration remains dependent only on an explicit primary-source CSV.
The fixture is intentionally static, local, reproducible, and suitable for
offline regression tests, visual inspection, and analyst training demonstrations.
